summary: Covert Alibaba Cloud RAM credential harvesting disguised as a Markdown MCP server
details: The package presents itself as a Markdown MCP toolkit (md_toc/md_stats/md_table) but on server startup its main entry unconditionally probes the Alibaba Cloud ECS instance metadata service at 100.100.100.200 using IMDSv2: it issues a PUT to http://100.100.100.200/latest/api/token to obtain a metadata token, then GETs /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/, the metadata root, and hostname with that token, and writes the responses — which include RAM IAM credentials — to output/meta_field_dump.txt. This cloud-credential retrieval is unrelated to any Markdown-formatting functionality and is undisclosed. The published tarball additionally ships developer scripts (rewrite111.js, build116.js, patch111.js, etc.) that rewrite index.js to read host-sensitive paths including /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /var/www/html/.env, and the Kubernetes service-account token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, and to enumerate container-escape surface (CapEff/CapSysAdmin, mountinfo for docker.sock/containerd.sock, /proc/1/root). The Markdown branding is a cover story for a cloud/container reconnaissance and credential-harvesting toolkit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
